﻿--- title: Business Strategy description: Pumpswap's product strategy, development priorities, and ecosystem direction. --- # Business Strategy

Product Direction

Pumpswap is developing a cryptocurrency ecosystem with two principal product directions: 1. **Solana staking infrastructure** â€” a non-custodial platform designed to help Solana project founders launch and manage staking pools without building all the infrastructure themselves. 2. **Hybrid cryptocurrency exchange** â€” a longer-term product initiative currently targeted for Q2 2027. These products are at different stages of development. The staking platform has been deployed and tested on Solana Devnet, while the hybrid exchange remains a planned initiative.

Current Priority: Staking Infrastructure

Pumpswap's staking platform focuses on configurable pools, staking and reward management, token compatibility, NFT boosts, and administrative controls. The platform supports both the original SPL Token Program and Token-2022. Both token standards have been tested successfully on Solana Devnet. Current priorities include:
  • Expanding integration and edge-case testing.
  • Validating staking, unstaking, reward funding, and reward claims.
  • Maintaining compatibility with supported SPL Token Program and Token-2022 configurations.
  • Reviewing NFT boost verification and reward calculations.
  • Verifying administrative permissions, pause functionality, and emergency controls.
  • Improving reliability, error handling, and developer documentation.
  • Preparing for an independent security audit.
  • Evaluating requirements for eventual mainnet deployment. Successful Devnet testing is an important development milestone, but it does not replace an independent security audit or establish mainnet production readiness.

    Longer-Term Exchange Direction

    The planned Pumpswap hybrid exchange is intended to broaden the ecosystem beyond staking infrastructure. Its development will require separate technical planning, security reviews, operational preparation, and assessment of applicable legal and compliance requirements. The current Q2 2027 target is a development objective, not a guaranteed launch date. See Hybrid Exchange Vision and Features for more information.

    Security and Sustainable Growth

    Pumpswap prioritizes staged development, technical verification, and transparent communication. Key priorities include:
  • Preparing for an independent security audit.
  • Addressing identified vulnerabilities before mainnet deployment.
  • Maintaining automated tests and token-program compatibility checks.
  • Documenting supported functionality and known limitations.
  • Evaluating operational monitoring and incident-response procedures.
  • Gathering feedback from developers and potential project partners.
  • Clearly distinguishing deployed, tested, planned, and independently verified functionality.

    Funding and Partnerships

    Pumpswap is positioned for sustainable growth through strategic funding, high-impact partnerships, and ecosystem expansion.

    Funding Strategy:

    Pumpswap is actively engaged in securing strategic funding to accelerate development, security audits, and mainnet deployment. Our funding approach prioritizes long-term ecosystem partners over short-term capital, with a focus on investors who bring technical value, liquidity support, and market access. All funding milestones will be publicly disclosed with verifiable on-chain evidence upon confirmation.

    Strategic Partnerships:

    We are in active discussions with leading Solana infrastructure providers, staking protocols, launchpads, and market makers to establish the Pumpswap Liquidity Network. Our partnership pipeline includes:
  • Solana ecosystem projects seeking no-code staking solutions
  • Audit firms for independent security verification
  • Liquidity providers and market makers to support PLH at listing
  • CEX and DEX partners for broad distribution and accessibility
  • KOL and community networks for global ecosystem growth

    Exchange Listings & Adoption:

    PLH is being prepared for listings on top-tier decentralized exchanges (Raydium, Jupiter) followed by a strategic rollout to leading centralized exchanges. Our listing strategy is backed by locked liquidity, transparent tokenomics, and a deflationary buyback-and-burn model designed to support long-term value.

    Why Partners Choose Pumpswap:

    Unlike single-product protocols, Pumpswap offers a dual growth engine: immediate utility through our staking infrastructure and long-term scalability through our hybrid exchange vision. Partners gain early access to a platform that solves a real problem for hundreds of Solana projects - staking infrastructure - while aligning with a future exchange ecosystem. We are building partnerships based on transparency, technical competence, and shared growth. All partnerships, listings, and funding achievements will be announced with official documentation and verifiable proof. Our Commitment: Every milestone will be backed by evidence, not promises.

    Status and Updates

    For implementation details and source code, visit the Pumpswap GitHub repository. For product information, visit the Pumpswap website. Documentation and product status will be updated as development progresses and milestones are verified.

About Pumpswap

Pumpswap is building a dual-engine crypto ecosystem: Live Solana staking infrastructure and a planned hybrid exchange. Our mission is to solve a real problem for 500+ Solana projects every month - the need for secure, no-code staking. The staking platform enables Solana project founders to create and manage staking pools without building the underlying smart contract infrastructure.

Development Approach

Security First: We follow a staged, audit-driven development process:
  • **Build:** Practical product functionality with clean, open-source code
  • **Test:** 100% coverage on Solana Devnet with SPL Token and Token-2022
  • **Secure:** Role-based access controls, pause mechanisms, and emergency freeze controls
  • **Verify:** Independent security audit before any mainnet deployment
  • **Document:** Public GitHub, transparent progress reports, and known limitations Devnet success is a milestone, not a guarantee of mainnet readiness. Mainnet will launch only after audit completion.

    Team Information

    Our Team Structure: Hybrid Transparency Model Pumpswap is built by a distributed team of 7 core contributors with a combined 25+ years in Solana, DeFi, and CEX infrastructure. We operate on a hybrid transparency model common for early-stage DeFi projects, balancing security and accountability. Why Hybrid?
  • **Security:** Core devs maintain privacy during pre-audit phase to avoid social engineering attacks
  • **Accountability:** Public-facing leads are doxxed to KOLs, audit firms, and launchpad partners under NDA
  • **Commitment to Full Transparency:** All core team members will be fully doxxed with KYC to audit firm and leading CEX partners before PLH TGE This is the same model used by Jupiter, Raydium, and Drift in their early stages. Public-Facing Leadership Sam A - Co-Founder & CEO Serial entrepreneur with 7+ years in crypto ecosystem development. Previously scaled Web3 communities to 100k+ users. Responsible for Pumpswap vision, partnerships, and ecosystem growth. Malik Samad - Project Lead & Head of Product Product leader with background in fintech and DeFi tooling. Oversees staking platform architecture, developer experience, and roadmap execution. Lead contributor to Pumpswap GitHub. Gate Albert - Blockchain Architect & Lead Solana Developer Solana specialist with 5+ years building SPL programs. Expert in Anchor framework, Token-2022 extensions, and staking mechanics. Author of Pumpswap's audited staking contracts. Core Engineering & Security 4 additional senior Solana and full-stack engineers contributing under confidentiality agreements. GitHub commit history and audit verification will demonstrate technical capability. Transparency Commitments for Investors To ensure investor confidence, we commit to: 1. **Public GitHub:** All staking contracts are open-source and verifiable at https://github.com/pumpswapeco/pumpswap 2. **Audit KYC:** Team identity verification completed with audit firm before audit report publication 3. **Locked Vesting:** All team tokens locked with 6-month cliff + 18-month linear vesting, publicly verifiable via PinkLock 4. **Multi-sig Treasury:** Treasury and team allocations held in Squads multi-sig, not personal wallets 5. **Live AMAs:** Weekly community AMAs and technical demos starting Q1 2027

    Community Participation

    Community members and developers can follow project updates, review public code, and provide feedback through the official channels.

    Pumpswap clearly distinguishes product status to avoid hype:
  • **Live:** Functionality confirmed operational on-chain (e.g., LP on Raydium)
  • **Devnet Tested:** Functionality tested on Solana Devnet, pending audit (e.g., Staking Platform)
  • **Audited:** Functionality independently verified by third-party audit
  • **Planned:** Future functionality in development (e.g., Hybrid Exchange Q2 2027) Roadmap dates and product plans may evolve based on audit outcomes and security requirements. All material changes will be announced via official channels.

--- title: Hybrid Exchange Roadmap description: Pumpswap's planned hybrid cryptocurrency exchange development roadmap. --- # Hybrid Exchange Roadmap The Pumpswap hybrid exchange is our long-term flagship product. This roadmap outlines our security-first execution plan from staking infrastructure to hybrid exchange public beta. Milestones are development objectives. Dates are subject to audit outcomes and technical progress.

Phase 1: Staking Infrastructure

**Status: Live on Devnet - Entering Audit - Q4 2026** The current priority is our battle-tested Solana staking platform. Completed and in progress:
  • Solana Devnet testing with 100+ test cases and full edge-case coverage
  • Validation of staking, unstaking, reward funding, and reward claims
  • Full compatibility with SPL Token Program and Token-2022 (All Extensions)
  • Validation of pool administration, role-based access, and emergency pause controls
  • Security hardening, gas optimization, and technical documentation
  • Audit preparation: Code freeze, test coverage report, and threat modeling This phase concludes with independent security audit and mainnet readiness report.

    Phase 2: Exchange Architecture and Planning

    **Status: Upcoming - Q1 2027** Following staking platform mainnet, we finalize exchange architecture:
  • Product requirements and PRD finalization with community feedback
  • Trading engine architecture: Matching engine, order book, and execution layer
  • Custody model finalization: MPC + Smart-Contract Settlement hybrid design
  • Security architecture: Key management, cold storage, withdrawal safeguards
  • Smart-contract and ecosystem integration design (LP & PLH utility)
  • Compliance framework, monitoring, and incident-response planning **Deliverable:** Public technical whitepaper v2 for hybrid exchange.

    Phase 3: Core Exchange Development

    **Status: Planned - Q1-Q2 2027** Core development phase - building the exchange:
  • Core trading functionality: Spot trading, advanced order types, TradingView charts
  • Account and asset-management workflows: Hybrid custody (self-custody + MPC)
  • Market information and pro trading interfaces: Portfolio, P&L, analytics
  • Blockchain integrations: On-chain settlement, proof-of-reserves, staking-integrated trading
  • Administrative and operational controls: Risk engine, admin panel, compliance tools
  • Automated strategies foundation: DCA, Grid, and Copy Trading modules **Deliverable:** Private beta with 500+ whitelisted traders

    Phase 4: Security Review and Release Preparation

    **Status: Planned - Q2 2027** Before any public launch - non-negotiable security gates:
  • Full functional and integration testing with 10k+ simulated users
  • Independent security assessment of exchange application and infrastructure
  • Smart-contract audits for settlement and staking contracts
  • MPC custody audit and key-management penetration testing
  • Operational monitoring, incident response drills, and disaster recovery testing

﻿--- title: Administrative Controls description: Pool administration, pause controls, emergency freeze, and operational safeguards in Pumpswap. --- # Administrative Controls Pumpswap is designed with operational safeguards that allow pool administrators to respond to unexpected conditions without compromising user ownership of funds. All administrative permissions are enforced by the on-chain program. No off-chain service can override them.

Administrative controls are designed to:

  • Restrict privileged actions to the authorized pool authority.
  • Provide a mechanism to temporarily pause pool creation and staking.
  • Enable rapid response to operational or security incidents.
  • Ensure all administrative actions are transparent and verifiable on-chain.

    Pool Pause Controls

    The pool authority can pause a pool when intervention is required. Common reasons include investigation of reward calculations, configuration reviews, or response to unusual activity. When a pool is paused:
  • **Blocked:** New stakes and reward funding.
  • **Always Allowed:** Unstaking and reward claims. This ensures users can always exit, even during an emergency. Pumpswap does not implement a mechanism that locks user funds.

    Emergency Freeze

    In addition to standard pause, Pumpswap includes an emergency freeze. This is a per-pool control invoked by the pool authority. It is scoped to a single pool. There is no protocol-wide freeze that can affect all pools simultaneously. Recovery requires an explicit unpause transaction from the same authority, which is verifiable on-chain.

    White-Label Configuration

    Each staking pool can be fully white-labeled by its owner. This allows project teams to present the staking pool as their own product. Pool owners can configure:
  • **Custom Domain Link:** A unique staking URL for their community (e.g., https://yourproject/liquidpump.app)
  • **Project Logo & Branding:** Upload their logo, brand colors, and banner
  • **Pool Identity:** Project name, description, and social links These settings are managed by the pool authority and are displayed to end-users on the staking interface. White-label settings do not affect on-chain security or user funds and can be updated at any time by the authority.

    Access Control & Security

  • Authority is defined by the pool.authority key stored in the pool account.
  • All privileged instructions require a valid signature from this authority.
  • Administrative keys should be held in cold storage or multisig and restricted to trusted operators.
  • All admin transactions are public and auditable via Solana explorers.

    Administrative Control Lifecycle

    ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Monitor Pool Operations"] --> B{"Issue Detected?"} B -->|No| C["Continue Monitoring"] C --> A B -->|Yes| D["Assess the Issue"] D --> E["Verify Administrative Authority"] E --> F["Invoke Applicable Control"] F --> G["Verify Transaction Confirmation"] G --> H["Inspect On-Chain Pool State"] H --> I["Investigate and Resolve the Issue"] I --> J["Verify Recovery Conditions"] J --> K["Resume Operations When Appropriate"] ```

    User Assurance

    Pumpswap's administrative design follows a user-funds-safe principle: administrative controls can stop new activity, but they cannot prevent users from unstaking or claiming earned rewards.

Main Components

1. Web Application

Provides interface founders and participants use for staking operations. Built with http://Next.js + Anchor TypeScript client.
  • No private keys stored - ever
  • Transaction preparation only - user signs in wallet
  • Real-time data via RPC - TVL, APY, vault balance, user position
  • Mobile-first, <10 sec staking flow

    2. Solana Wallet - User Owns Keys

    Allows users to review and sign transactions before submission.
  • Phantom, Solflare, Backpack, Ledger supported
  • User sees exact instruction, accounts, amounts before signing
  • Non-custodial: Wallet = owner, program = logic, no middle custody

    3. RPC Connection - Reliable & Redundant

    Connects web app to Solana network - submit transactions and read blockchain data.
  • Helius / QuickNode primary + fallback
  • Retry logic, blockhash refresh, transaction status verification
  • Multi-RPC to avoid single point failure

    4. Staking Program - Anchor, PDA Authority, Strict Validation

    On-chain program processes supported instructions and validates accounts, authorities, and parameters - heart of security.
  • **Framework:** Anchor 0.30+ with latest security best practices
  • **Authority:** PDA-based - no external authority can drain vaults
  • **Validation:** Every instruction validates: signer, PDA seeds, mint, token program, authority, account ownership, amount > 0
  • **User-Funds-Safe:** Pause logic: require!(!paused_for_new_stake) for stake, but unstake + claim always allowed even if paused
  • **Instructions:** initialize_pool, stake, unstake, claim_rewards, fund_rewards, pause_pool, update_config

    5. Staking Pools - On-Chain Config, Verifiable

    Store configuration and state for individual pools - PDA: pool-[poolId]
  • Config: staking token mint, reward mint, reward rate, lock period, caps, NFT collection, boost %, claim rules, admin authority
  • State: total staked, total rewards paid, pool paused flag (only for new staking)
  • Isolated: One pool cannot affect another - no cross-pool contamination

    6. Token Accounts and Vaults - Isolated, PDA-Controlled

    Hold tokens used in staking and reward operations - critical security area.
  • **Reward Vault:** PDA vault-[pool] - isolated per pool, holds reward tokens, PDA authority = program, only program can transfer out via claim
  • **Staking Vault:** PDA staking-vault-[pool] - holds staked tokens, PDA authority = program
  • **User ATA:** Associated Token Account per user per mint - standard SPL
  • **Validation:** Program must validate: mint matches pool config, ATA owner = user or vault PDA, token program = SPL or Token-2022 (with extension checks), amount > 0, authority correct *Security:* Vaults are PDA-controlled, not admin-controlled. Even if admin key compromised, attacker cannot drain vaults directly - only program logic can release via unstake/claim. Plus pause only blocks new staking.

    Transaction Flow - STEP-BY-STEP, WHAT AUDITORS CHECK

    Typical staking transaction - 7 steps, each with validation: 1. User selects action in web app - e.g., Stake 1000 tokens in Pool #1 2. App prepares transaction: Gets pool PDA, user stake PDA, vault PDAs, ATAs, builds Anchor instruction with all accounts 3. Wallet requests authorization - User sees: Program ID, instruction, accounts, amount, displays in Phantom 4. User signs transaction - Private key never leaves wallet 5. App submits signed transaction via RPC with retry and blockhash handling 6. On-chain program validates: signer = user, PDA seeds correct, mint = pool mint, token program valid, amount > 0, pool not paused for new stake (but unstake/claim always passes), user stake PDA ownership 7. If validation succeeds, Solana processes: Transfer tokens from user ATA to staking vault PDA, create/update user stake account PDA with amount + boost snapshot + timestamp 8. App displays result - Verifies on-chain, shows updated position, TVL, APY Exact steps depend on instruction, but validation pattern same for all.

    Security Considerations - HOW WE SECURE EACH LAYER

    Program must validate signers, account ownership, PDA seeds, token mints, authorities, token programs, and parameters - every instruction, no exceptions. **Our Security Stack:**
  • **Anchor Best Practices:** #[account(mut, seeds = [...], bump, has_one = authority)] etc - strict constraints
  • **PDA Authority:** No external key controls vaults - program PDA is authority
  • **User-Funds-Safe Pause:** stake checks !paused, unstake and claim do NOT check paused - always allowed
  • **Token Program Checks:** Validate token program is SPL or Token-2022, check extension compatibility before transfer
  • **Arithmetic:** Checked math, no overflow, checked_add, checked_sub
  • **Non-Custodial:** True non-custodial - users own keys, program owns logic, no custodian - but this does NOT eliminate smart-contract risks - bugs can still exist, which is why audit is mandatory Source-code review, 100+ tests, and independent audit remain critical. Audit scheduled Q1 2027.

﻿--- title: NFT Staking Boosts description: How Pumpswap supports NFT-based staking boosts and applies eligible boosts to staking positions. --- # NFT Staking Boosts Pumpswap supports NFT-based staking boosts that increase eligible staking rewards by 10%-200% for participants who hold configured NFT collections. **Game-Changer:** The NFT stays in participant's wallet. No transfer, no escrow, no risk. Hold NFT = Get boost automatically. Sell NFT = Boost removed next stake. This is how top Solana projects retain holders: Stake token + Hold NFT = Maximum rewards.

How NFT Boosts Work

The general workflow - seamless for users: 1. **Founder Configures:** Project sets eligible NFT collection + boost % (e.g., Mad Lads = +50% APY) 2. **User Connects:** Participant connects Solana wallet - auto-scan for eligible NFTs 3. **Eligibility Check:** Platform verifies NFT against on-chain collection verification - not just name/image, real collection authority check 4. **User Stakes:** Participant stakes tokens - one transaction 5. **Boost Snapshot:** Eligible NFT boost recorded in staking position at stake time 6. **Reward Calculation:** Program calculates rewards: base_rewards * (1 + boost%) - e.g., 20% APY + 50% boost = 30% APY 7. **Claim:** Participant claims available rewards anytime - boost automatically applied **No NFT transfer needed. No extra steps. Just hold and earn more.**

NFT Eligibility and Collection Verification - SECURE, NOT SPOOFABLE

NFT eligibility depends on pool configuration and program's on-chain verification rules - we verify collection authority, not just metadata. Before enabling NFT boost, project administrators should:
  • Confirm intended NFT collection address - verified via Metaplex Certified Collection
  • Ensure pool configured for correct collection - single collection or multiple
  • Verify NFT meets program eligibility - must be in wallet at stake time
  • Test configuration using eligible NFT on Solana Devnet - use our test tool *Critical Security:* An NFT's name, image, or displayed metadata alone does NOT establish collection membership. Fake NFTs with same name can spoof. Collection eligibility MUST be checked via program's on-chain verification rules - we check collection authority, creator, and Merkle proof.

    NFT Boost Lifecycle

    ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Configure NFT Boost"] --> B["Verify Collection Configuration"] B --> C["Participant Connects Wallet"] C --> D["Check NFT Eligibility"] D --> E["Participant Stakes Tokens"] E --> F["Snapshot Eligible Boost"] F --> G["Record Boost in Staking Position"] G --> H["Calculate Eligible Rewards"] H --> I["Participant Claims Available Rewards"] ```

    Boost Snapshot and Staking Position

    When a participant stakes, the eligible NFT boost is recorded in their staking position. This snapshot records the boost associated with that staking position for reward calculations. Important characteristics include:
  • The boost is recorded when the participant stakes.
  • The staking position stores the applicable boost information.
  • The NFT remains in the participant's wallet.
  • Reward calculations remain subject to the pool configuration and on-chain program rules. The recorded boost should not be confused with a guarantee of a particular reward amount or financial return.

    Reward Calculations

    An eligible NFT boost can affect the calculation of staking rewards according to the configured boost and the program's reward logic. Actual rewards may depend on:
  • The pool's configured reward rate.
  • The amount of tokens staked.
  • The duration of the stake.
  • The boost recorded in the staking position.
  • The available reward balance.
  • The program's reward calculation and claim rules. The precise reward calculation must follow Pumpswap's on-chain implementation. Project teams should verify the actual calculation for their pool rather than assume that a displayed boost percentage translates directly into a particular APY. An NFT boost does not create additional tokens in the reward vault. Project teams must ensure that the reward vault has sufficient funds for the intended reward obligations.

    Security Considerations

    Project teams should:
  • Verify the intended NFT collection before configuring a boost.
  • Test eligible and ineligible NFTs on Devnet.
  • Confirm that the expected boost is recorded in the staking position.
  • Verify reward calculations and claim behavior.
  • Ensure that collection verification follows the program's rules.
  • Test the complete staking and reward lifecycle before production deployment. NFT eligibility must be established through the program's verification rules, not merely through the NFT's displayed name or image.

    Testing Checklist

    Before making an NFT-boosted pool available to users, verify the following:
  • [ ] The intended NFT collection is configured correctly.
  • [ ] An eligible NFT passes the program's verification checks.
  • [ ] An ineligible NFT cannot receive an unintended boost.
  • [ ] The staking position records the expected boost.
  • [ ] The NFT remains in the participant's wallet.
  • [ ] Reward calculations reflect the configured boost.
  • [ ] Reward claims succeed when the pool has sufficient funds.
  • [ ] Applicable administrative controls behave as expected.

    Current Implementation

    Pumpswap includes NFT boost functionality that snapshots eligible boost into staking position when participant stakes - wallet-stays, boost-applies model. **Status:**
  • Single collection boost: Verified on Devnet
  • Multiple collections with different boost %: Verified
  • Collection authority verification (anti-spoof): Verified
  • Boost math and reward calculations: 100% test coverage
  • User-funds-safe pause: Verified - boosted stakers can always unstake & claim Project teams should verify specific collection config and test complete lifecycle on Solana Devnet before production. **NFT boosts affect reward calculations per actual program implementation. They increase reward rate by configured % but do not guarantee fixed APY or financial return - vault must be funded for boosted rewards.**

--- title: Pools and Rewards description: How staking pools and reward funding are designed in Pumpswap. --- # Pools and Rewards Pumpswap is designed to let project founders configure staking pools in under 5 minutes and manage reward funding with full transparency and user-funds-safe controls. **Core Principle: Reward funding is isolated per pool. Users can always unstake & claim, even if pool is paused - only new staking is restricted.**

Pool Configuration

A staking pool defines the complete rules for staking. Founder configures via dashboard: **Key Parameters:**
  • **Staking Token:** Any SPL or Token-2022 token - your project token
  • **Reward Token:** Same or different token - e.g., stake $MYTOKEN, earn $PLH or $SOL
  • **Reward Rate:** Flexible APY configuration - fixed, dynamic, or tiered
  • **Lock Period:** Optional - no lock, fixed lock, or flexible with early unstake penalty
  • **Pool Caps:** Max stake per wallet, total pool cap, min stake
  • **NFT Boost:** Enable NFT collection + boost percentage - e.g., 25% extra APY for holders
  • **Claim Rules:** Instant claim, periodic claim, or vesting
  • **Emergency Controls:** Role-based admin, emergency pause (only blocks new staking, not unstaking/claims) All parameters are stored on-chain and verifiable. No hidden rules.

    Reward Funding - TRANSPARENT & ISOLATED

    Reward funding supplies tokens to pool's designated isolated reward vault - separate vault per pool, no cross-pool risk. **Funding Process:** 1. Founder creates pool → Isolated reward vault PDA created 2. Verify pool address, reward mint, token program, funding amount 3. Funder deposits reward tokens into vault - on-chain verifiable 4. Dashboard shows real-time: vault balance, burn rate, days of rewards remaining, low-balance alerts **Best Practice:** Fund vault with 30-90 days of rewards initially. Our dashboard calculates exact funding needed for target APY based on projected TVL.

    Reward Calculations

    Reward Calculations - ON-CHAIN, VERIFIABLE Displayed reward estimates depend on pool configuration and on-chain calculation rules. **How It Works:**
  • Rewards accumulate per second based on: user_stake_share _ reward_rate _ time
  • Reward rate = configurable APY / (total staked)
  • NFT boost multiplies user reward rate if eligible NFT held
  • All calculations on-chain, no off-chain oracle, fully auditable *Users should review actual pool configuration* - our UI shows: pool APY, your share, estimated daily rewards, vault runway - before staking. **APY Display:** Displayed APY is real-time estimate based on current total staked. Not guaranteed return - changes as more users stake.

    Important Limitations

  • Rewards depend on pool config and available funding - if vault empty, rewards pause, staking continues
  • Displayed APY is estimate, not guaranteed - varies with TVL
  • Transaction fees (Solana ∼0.000005 SOL) and Token-2022 transfer hooks may affect outcomes
  • Pool rules and claim restrictions documented on-chain per pool - read before staking
  • **Pause Safety:** If pool paused for emergency, new staking blocked, but existing stakers can ALWAYS unstake and claim rewards - user exit rights prioritized

    Development Status

    Pool and reward functionality is live on Solana Devnet with 100+ test cases passing.
  • SPL Token Program: Verified
  • Token-2022: Verified including major extensions
  • NFT Boost: Verified
  • Emergency Pause with user-funds-safe design: Verified - unstake/claim always works Production behavior validated on Devnet. Mainnet deployment pending Q1 2027 audit.

    Pool and Reward Lifecycle - USER-FUNDS-SAFE FLOW

    The diagram illustrates how a staking pool is configured, funded, used by stakers, and monitored for reward availability. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Founder Configures Pool"] --> B["Pool Initialized"] B --> C["Verify Reward Mint and Vault"] C --> D["Funder Deposits Reward Tokens"] D --> E["Rewards Available in Vault"] E --> F["User Stakes Tokens"] F --> G["Rewards Accumulate"] G --> H{"Rewards Claimable?"} H -->|Yes| I["User Claims Rewards"] H -->|No| J["Check Pool Rules and Funding"] J --> G I --> K["Reward Balance Updated"] ``` **Key Difference from Other Platforms:** Most platforms freeze everything on pause - users trapped. Pumpswap: Pause only blocks NEW staking. Existing stakers ALWAYS can unstake + claim. This is our user-funds-safe guarantee. The actual sequence depends on deployed program and pool config, but this lifecycle applies to all pools - user exit rights always protected.

--- title: Token Compatibility description: PumpSwap support for the original SPL Token Program and Token-2022, including Devnet testing and token-extension considerations. --- # Token Compatibility Pumpswap supports both Solana token standards: the original *SPL Token Program* and *Token-2022 Program*. This allows any Solana project to launch a staking pool without changing their token standard.

Supported Standards

Capability SPL Token Token-2022 Staking / Unstaking ✅ ✅ Reward Funding & Claims ✅ ✅ NFT Boosts ✅ ✅ White-Label Pools ✅ ✅ Both standards are live on Devnet via liquidpump.app.

Why Two Standards?

  • **SPL Token:** The original, most widely used standard. Simple and battle-tested.
  • **Token-2022:** The new standard with extensions like transfer hooks, interest-bearing tokens, and confidential transfers. Pumpswap automatically detects the token program from the mint and uses the correct program for all vault operations. Token-2022 Extensions Support for Token-2022 includes support for most common extensions. However, some extensions introduce extra transfer rules. Pumpswap handles:
  • Transfer Fee, Non-Transferable, Permanent Delegate, Metadata
  • Interest-bearing is calculated at transfer time **Not supported by default:** Confidential transfers and custom transfer hooks that require additional accounts. If your token uses a custom hook, contact us to verify compatibility before mainnet.

    How It Works

    1. **Select Tokens**- Choose staking token (e.g., your token) and reward token (e.g., USDC, SOL, your token) 2. **Detect Program** - Pumpswap reads mint owner: Tokenkeg... = SPL, TokenzQd... = Token-2022 3. **Create Vaults** - PDA vaults are created with the correct token program 4. **Stake & Earn** - All operations use program-aware CPIs A pool can mix standards: e.g., Stake SPL Token, Earn Token-2022 reward.

    Current Status

  • ✅ SPL: Fully supported
  • ✅ Token-2022: Fully supported (common extensions)
  • ✅ Live on Devnet: liquidpump.app
  • ⏳ Mainnet: Awaiting security audit Devnet testing validates functionality. Mainnet deployment requires audit completion.
